This doesn't prohibit you from removing comments that break the rules, and 'doxxing' of a voat user is breaking one of those rules.

As a personal opinion:
Publicly available information is not doxxing - unless the source that made it public did so via unauthorized means. ie: Hacking an account or other not-normally-public method of information finding.
Repeating someone else who 'hacked doxx' is not protected, even though it is now in the public eye.

Information gathered from public legal documents such as business registrations, permits etc is not doxxing as the person identified by it is knowingly giving public information and understands the protection of privacy does not apply.

Comments that contain both publicly available information AND calls for violence to the person identified should be removed, with a moderator note explaining the removal in the public comment chain.
In the case of threads only the violence advocating comments should be removed - not the whole thread.

And before it happens, any new user account created after a "doxxing" comment has no standing to claim doxxing of a voat user - as not creating an account and commenting is the best way to avoid confirmation and also pitchforks.
Meaning, if a comment is posted using publicly available material that formally makes a clear connection between a person and pedophile activity is made, an account with a creation timestamp after the comment timestamp cannot request removal by claiming to be the identified person and a voat user in order to trigger the rule permitting deleting of comments.
